# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim / Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (confirmed via DHCP Option 12 and NBNS name registration `DESKTOP-ES9F3ML<00>/<20>`) |
| AD domain | WIN11OFFICE.COM (DC/LDAP server 10.1.21.2, `WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com`) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **gwyatt** (seen as Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.1.21.58 and DC 10.1.21.2, realm WIN11OFFICE.COM) |

Only 10.1.21.58 in the /24 resolved or connected to the malicious infrastructure below; 10.1.21.2 traffic on the same domains is just the client's DNS server relaying answers. No other internal host is implicated.

## 2. Malware Family / Attribution

**Attribution: BEHAVIORAL, not signature-confirmed.** No Suricata/IDS alert export or AV log was provided alongside the pcap — only the raw capture — and all payload transfer occurs inside TLS 1.3 (with Encrypted Client Hello to the Cloudflare-fronted domains), so no file could be carved or hashed from the wire.

Based on observed behavior, this is a **malvertising/TDS-fronted stealer-delivery chain**, consistent with the "fake-download-portal → cloaking/fingerprint gate → scareware/security-alert landing" pattern used by ClickFix-style and TDS-gated stealer campaigns (e.g., the class of loaders distributed via Lumma/Vidar-style operations). Key behavioral evidence:

- A domain named to impersonate a file-hosting hub (`filemegahab4.sbs` / `megafilehub4.lat`) delivered a **16 MB HTTPS payload** to the victim browser immediately after the redirect chain began.
- A separate C2-like endpoint (`whitepepper.su`) ran a bot-registration/fingerprinting API (`/api/set_agent`) that collected full browser/device fingerprints (WebGL renderer, canvas fingerprint, hardware concurrency, user-agent for both Chrome and Edge) and exfiltrated them via repeated `act=log` POSTs — classic cloaking/bot-filtering behavior used to gate malicious payloads from sandboxes/researchers.
- The chain terminates at `holiday-forever.cc` and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (name itself impersonates a security/firewall warning), the typical shape of a fake-alert/scareware landing page.

No specific branded family name can be asserted with confidence without the decrypted payload or a hash/YARA/AV match.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in captured traffic)

### Redirect / delivery chain (chronological, relative to capture start)
| Time (s) | Domain | Resolved IP | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45.3 | `hiyter.com` | 104.21.22.231 (Cloudflare) | Entry point of chain; TLS uses ECH (outer SNI `cloudflare-ech.com`) |
| 46.0 | `media.megafilehub4.lat` | 104.21.48.156 | 217 KB exchanged |
| 48.3 | `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` | 104.21.46.67 (also 172.67.136.13) | **16 MB downloaded to victim over TLS in 22 s** — the likely payload drop |
| 90.5 | `whooptm.cyou` | 62.72.32.156 | Intermediate redirector |
| 92.5–122.0 | `whitepepper.su` | **153.92.1.49** | Fingerprinting/bot-tracking C2 (see below); ~50+ short-lived TLS/HTTP sessions, plus one 1.4 MB upload burst at 118.3s |
| 123.0 | `holiday-forever.cc` | 80.97.160.24 | 125 KB — landing page |
| 126.5–127.7 | `communicationfirewall-security.cc` | 104.21.9.36 (also 172.67.141.109) | 107 KB + 46 KB — final scareware/alert landing page |

### C2 / tracking endpoint — plaintext HTTP evidence (port 80, `whitepepper.su`, 153.92.1.49)
- `GET http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome` → 200, serves a JS fingerprinting payload (WebGL renderer/canvas fingerprint/hardware/user-agent collection).
- `POST http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` → 200, body contains the full JSON fingerprint (`timestamp`, `system`, `webgl`, `canvas` fields — confirmed decoded from capture).
- Same sequence repeated with `agent=Edge` at t≈103s (malware/site re-checks under a second browser identity).
- `GET /favicon.ico` → 404 (both instances).
- Fixed bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`; fixed session token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`.

### C2 / TDS endpoints (IP:port)
- `153.92.1.49:80` and `153.92.1.49:443` — whitepepper.su (persistent beaconing/fingerprint C2)
- `104.21.46.67:443` (and `172.67.136.13:443`) — arch.filemegahab4.sbs (payload host)
- `104.21.48.156:443` (and `172.67.154.67:443`) — media.megafilehub4.lat
- `62.72.32.156:443` — whooptm.cyou
- `80.97.160.24:443` — holiday-forever.cc
- `104.21.9.36:443` (and `172.67.141.109:443`) — communicationfirewall-security.cc
- `104.21.22.231:443` (and `172.67.207.145:443`) — hiyter.com

### Malicious domains
`hiyter.com`, `media.megafilehub4.lat`, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, `whooptm.cyou`, `whitepepper.su`, `holiday-forever.cc`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`

### Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

### Transferred files / hashes
None recoverable. All traffic beyond the two plaintext `whitepepper.su` HTTP exchanges above is TLS 1.3-encrypted (with ECH on the Cloudflare-fronted domains: `hiyter.com`, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`), so the 16 MB file delivered from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` and the 1.4 MB upload burst to `whitepepper.su` at t≈118s cannot be carved or hashed from this capture. No SHA256 or filename is present anywhere in cleartext traffic.

## 4. Summary of Activity
Host DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58, user `gwyatt`) browsed to `hiyter.com`, was redirected through a chain of malvertising/TDS domains, and downloaded a 16 MB file over TLS from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` — most likely the point of malware acquisition, though its contents cannot be verified from ciphertext. The browser then repeatedly checked in with a fingerprinting/bot-tracking API at `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49), submitting full device/browser fingerprints under a persistent bot ID/token and eventually uploading a 1.4 MB data burst, before landing on a page at `communicationfirewall-security.cc` styled as a security/firewall alert. This is consistent with a TDS-gated stealer/scareware delivery campaign; final malware family cannot be named with certainty absent payload recovery or an AV/IDS signature hit.
